attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, presented as his self-assessment.

semantics.note: Faithful restatement of a retrospective report of his own surprise. It names no prior forecast, company set, or valuation measure.

contract.note: The contract correctly finds the claim untestable as stated. Any test would need a baseline expectation and a valuation series that the speaker did not supply.

reviews.rationale: This is a statement about Marcus's own past expectation and surprise, with no identified forecast, endpoint, company set or valuation metric. Market data cannot show what he privately expected, and choosing one earlier post as the baseline would add a commitment he did not make here. The packet cites no evidence items. Not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: A present-tense claim of high and rising training cost. 'Ridiculously' is evaluative emphasis. The normalised wording keeps both parts.

contract.note: The plain reading (frontier training cost per run is large and rising) is the ordinary meaning in a passage about competing leading labs. It properly excludes cost per unit of capability and the Claude family figure.

evidence.note: Epoch AI's trends page (independent, Feb 2026) estimates frontier training costs rising about 3.5x per year, within the contract interval.
Epoch's estimate of about $490M for Grok 4 (2025) shows one frontier run's scale. It is a single-company estimate and illustrates the claim rather than measuring the trend.

reviews.rationale: An independent Epoch AI estimate, available Feb 2026, finds frontier training costs climbing about 3.5x a year, and a 2025 frontier run is estimated near $490M. That shows both large cost and an upward trend during the 2023–2026 interval. The packet reports no contrary measurement. The trend is an estimate and runs only to early 2026, but that is enough on the plain reading.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A compound retrospective observation with three parts (lower prices, higher competition, elusive profits). The 'since 2023' framing matches 'three years later'.

contract.note: The readings of prices (capability-matched), competition (credible suppliers) and profits (net, latest quarter) are ordinary. However, the speaker gave no basket, company set or accounting basis.

evidence.note: Epoch AI (Mar 2025) finds inference prices at fixed capability fell sharply. This supports the direction of the price part, but the data stop well before publication.
The 2026 AI Index finds the gap between top models shrinking. That is technical convergence, not a full measure of market competition.
Anthropic's filing (via a mirror) reports large net losses for the nine months to Sep 2026, much of it from fair-value changes. It covers one company and a period other than the contract quarter.

reviews.rationale: Each part points in the speaker's direction, but none meets the contract. The price data end in Mar 2025. The competition evidence measures benchmark convergence, not market competition. The profit evidence covers one company over nine months, mostly fair-value losses, not representative July–September 2026 results on a common basis. The packet does not settle the compound claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The wording is faithful. But 'is a sign that' infers that rehiring reflects AI shortfalls. The contract rightly treats this as causal, not a plain observation.

contract.note: Reading the claim as 'rehiring after AI claims reflects AI performance shortfalls' is fair, and it rightly does not require that AI be useless. The speaker named no companies beyond Klarna and gave no benchmark for the hype.

evidence.note: Klarna's Feb 2024 press release shows its earlier claims of human-level performance. It is company promotion and validates nothing.
Klarna confirmed to CIO (May 2025) that it hired two agents in a pilot. This supports the rehiring fact but frames them as complementing AI, not replacing it.
In SEC correspondence (Jul 2025), Klarna denies that the CEO's comments concerned AI quality. This is a self-interested company statement, not an independent finding.

reviews.rationale: Klarna did resume some human hiring after its AI claims, but only a two-person pilot. The causal link to AI shortfalls is disputed: reports cite the CEO on lower quality, while Klarna's filing denies the link. Neither side gives an independent performance finding, and the underlying interview was not readable. The broader claim about other companies is unsupported in the packet. Unresolved.
